newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Jan. 28

BERLIN - Switzerland's ambassador to the United States resigned following disclosure of a confidential strategy paper he wrote last month urging his government to "wage war" against allegations that Swiss banks had failed to account for missing assets of Holocaust victims.

WASHINGTON - Senior Clinton administration officials said they are growing increasingly concerned about the health of Russian President Boris Yeltsin because his recovery from open-heart surgery in November is going more slowly than they had expected.

PARIS - The museums of France possess 1,965 works of art seized or purchased by the Nazis from French owners, most of them Jewish, during the World War II occupation, according to a report made public by Le Monde newspaper.

WASHINGTON - Only months after Congress turned control of welfare over to the states, legislatures around the country are considering whether to hand off responsibility for the poor once again, this time to county and local governments.

SANTA MONICA, Calif. - In his last closing arguments, O.J. Simpson's lawyer asked jurors to conclude that crooked police planted a bloody glove at Simpson's mansion and dribbled damming blood evidence from Simpson and two murder victims on the defendant's socks and his car, and at the murder scene.

HOUSTON - A Texas doctor, one of the best known and most controversial figures in the field of alternative cancer treatments, says his long legal battle with the federal government is a matter of life and death.
